newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh to issue bond to fund industry.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh to issue bond to fund industry.

text.p: Bangladesh decided on Sunday to issue a new bond to raise funds for industrial financing at a time when the banks have less money to lend because of mounting bad loans, finance ministry officials said.
They said a total of 10 billion taka ($227.3 million) would be realised in the next year through selling the bond to the general public.
"The amount would subsequently reach up to 20 billion taka," one official told Reuters, adding that the central bank would start selling the bond in next one month.
"The bond would offer interest rates higher than the banks give on deposits. We hope it will be attractive to people," a central bank official said.

Officials said the government was carrying out negotiations with international funding agencies, including the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank (ADB), for loans to private industrial entrepreneurs.
"We hope we would be able to arrange $500 million from external sources," one official said.
Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria had said earlier this month that a number of other schemes were being considered to mobilise funds for the industrial sector.
The Finance Minister said that revenues to be raised by selling state-owned enterprises (SOEs) would be ploughed back in the manufacturing sector as industrial financing.
The government has listed 65 SOEs for immediate privatisation.
Huge deafulted loans, totalling about 150 billion taka ($3.4 billion), have caused liquidity problems in banks, squeezing their capability to provide loans for industrial ventures.
